topics.title: Navigating the Official Portal and Interactive Action Tabs
topics.summary: Step-by-step guidance on navigating the official portal options, action tabs, and support modules.
topics.content: To navigate the official e-Visa portal (indianvisaonline.gov.in): 1) To start a new application, click 'Apply here for e-visa' on the bottom action bar or central panel. 2) To see an example form before applying, click 'Sample e-Visa Application'. 3) To resume an unfinished form, select 'Complete Partially Filled Application Form' and enter your Application ID. 4) To check payment status or finish a pending payment, select 'Verify Payment/Pay e-Visa Fee'. 5) To track your application progress, click 'Check your Visa Status'. 6) Once approved, select 'Print e-Visa Application' to download your Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA). 7) If you receive an email regarding document errors, select 'Reupload Data' to upload revised files. 8) Use the left-side panel to view eligible countries, step-by-step instructions, FAQs, authorized entry checkposts, and bank helpdesk numbers.

topics.title: Dedicated Application Portal for Afghan Nationals
topics.summary: Afghan nationals must apply through a specialized sub-portal and are excluded from the standard e-Visa workflow.
topics.content: Afghan passport holders are not permitted to use the standard e-Visa application portal. Under Ministry of Home Affairs directives, Afghan nationals must submit their online visa applications exclusively through the specialized AFGHAN Portal at https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/avisa. Submissions made on the general portal by Afghan citizens will be invalidated.

topics.title: Mandatory Digital e-Arrival Card Pre-Departure Filing
topics.summary: Foreign travelers and OCI cardholders must submit an online e-Arrival Card within 72 hours prior to arrival.
topics.content: All foreign nationals and Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholders must complete and submit a digital e-Arrival Card online within 72 hours prior to their arrival in India. This disembarkation filing can be completed via boi.gov.in, indianvisaonline.gov.in/earrival, or through the official 'Indian Visa Su-Swagatam' mobile app. This card records arrival information and does not replace a valid visa.

topics.title: Application Timeline and Advance Submission Windows
topics.summary: Apply at least 4 days prior to arrival. Medical, attendant, and conference categories allow up to a 120-day submission window.
topics.content: Eligible applicants must apply online at least 4 calendar days in advance of their planned arrival date in India. For 30-day e-Tourist and e-Business visas, applications must be submitted within this minimum 4-day window. For e-Medical, e-Medical Attendant, and e-Conference visas, applicants can submit applications up to 120 days in advance of their selected arrival date.

topics.title: Passport Validity Standards and Blank Page Requirements
topics.summary: Passports must have at least 6 months remaining validity from the arrival date and a minimum of two blank pages.
topics.content: An applicant's ordinary passport must have at least six (6) months of remaining validity from the date of arrival in India. Additionally, the passport must contain at least two (2) blank pages for physical entry and exit stamps applied by immigration officers at checkpoints.

topics.title: Digital Photograph Upload Specifications
topics.summary: Photo uploads must be square JPEG files between 10 KB and 1 MB, showing a front view on a white background without spectacles.
topics.content: The photo upload must be in JPEG format, sized between 10 KB and 1 MB. Dimensions must maintain a 1:1 square aspect ratio (minimum 350x350 pixels). The image must show a full frontal view of the face with eyes open, natural expression, centered head, plain white or light-colored background, no shadows, no borders, and strictly without spectacles or eyewear.

topics.title: Passport Bio Page Document Upload Rules
topics.summary: Passport biographical pages must be uploaded as PDF files between 10 KB and 300 KB, clearly showing personal details and the MRZ zone.
topics.content: Applicants must upload a clear PDF scan of their passport biographical page. File size must be between 10 KB and 300 KB. The scan must be uncropped, clearly legible, and show all personal details, photograph, signature, and the complete Machine Readable Zone (MRZ) across the bottom.

topics.title: Required Supporting Documents and Language Standards
topics.summary: Mandatory uploads include a photo and passport scan, plus category-specific supporting documents in PDF format and English.
topics.content: All applicants must upload a JPEG photo and a PDF scan of their passport bio page. Depending on the visa sub-category, additional supporting documents are required in PDF format (10 KB to 300 KB): business cards or invitation letters for e-Business; hospital letters for e-Medical; and event clearances for e-Conference. All supporting documents must be in English or accompanied by an official English translation.

topics.title: Core Four-Step e-Visa Application Workflow
topics.summary: The application process consists of four steps: online form submission, fee payment, electronic authorization issuance, and airport stamping.
topics.content: The e-Visa issuance process follows a 4-step sequence: Step 1) Apply Online by filling demographic data and uploading JPEG photo and PDF passport scan; Step 2) Pay e-Visa Fee Online using credit card, debit card, or payment wallet; Step 3) Receive ETA Online via email upon government approval; Step 4) Fly to India by printing the Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) and presenting it at immigration for biometric verification and passport stamping.

topics.title: e-Tourist Visa Sub-Categories and Permitted Activities
topics.summary: e-Tourist visas are available in 30-day, 1-year, and 5-year validity options for tourism, social visits, yoga, and short informal courses.
topics.content: The e-Tourist visa offers three options: 1) 30-Day e-Tourist Visa featuring double entry, non-extendable and non-convertible; 2) 1-Year (365-Day) e-Tourist Visa with multiple entries and continuous stay up to 90 days (180 days for US, UK, Canada, Japan citizens); 3) 5-Year e-Tourist Visa with multiple entries subject to identical stay limits. Permitted activities include tourism, sightseeing, casual social visits, short non-certified yoga programs, and non-formal courses under 6 months duration.

topics.title: e-Business Visa Regulations and Continuous Stay Limits
topics.summary: e-Business visas provide 1-year multiple entry access for commercial visits, requiring FRRO registration if continuous stay exceeds 180 days.
topics.content: The e-Business Visa (e-B1 V) is valid for 1 year (365 days) from the ETA grant date and allows multiple entries. Continuous stay during each business visit is capped at 180 days. If business operations require a continuous stay exceeding 180 days, mandatory registration with the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO/FRO) must take place within two weeks after the 180-day mark. Uploading a business card or host invitation letter is required.

topics.title: e-Medical and e-Medical Attendant Visa Protocols
topics.summary: e-Medical visas permit triple-entry treatment in Indian hospitals, with up to two attendant visas granted per medical patient.
topics.content: e-Medical Visas are granted to foreign patients seeking medical treatment in recognized Indian hospitals, allowing triple entries within a 60-day or 1-year framework. Up to two (2) e-Medical Attendant Visas (e-M2 V) can be granted co-terminus against a single primary e-Medical Visa holder. Applicants must upload an official letter from the treating hospital in India on its letterhead specifying tentative admission dates and medical purpose.

topics.title: e-Conference Visa Rules and Mandatory Clearances
topics.summary: e-Conference visas allow 30-day single entry for government-organized conferences, requiring MEA and MHA clearances.
topics.content: The e-Conference Visa permits single-entry travel to attend international conferences, seminars, or workshops organized by Indian government ministries, public sector undertakings, or recognized institutions. Valid for 30 days from entry. Mandatory uploads include an invitation letter from the organizer, Political Clearance from the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), and Event Clearance from the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

topics.title: e-Student and e-Family Visa Category Rules
topics.summary: e-Student visas cover short-term academic courses, while e-Family visas grant entry privileges for accompanying family members.
topics.content: The e-Student Visa applies to foreign nationals pursuing short-term structured academic courses or training at recognized Indian institutions. The e-Family Visa (e-SX V) provides entry privileges valid for up to 1 year with multiple entries for eligible family members joining primary visa holders or foreign residents in India, subject to uploading proof of relationship.

topics.title: e-Transit and e-Miscellaneous Visa Conditions
topics.summary: e-Transit visas allow 15-day double-entry transit, while e-Miscellaneous visas cover short production investment visits.
topics.content: The e-Transit Visa is intended for travelers transiting through India to a third country, offering a stay of up to 15 days with double-entry privileges upon presenting confirmed onward travel tickets. The e-Miscellaneous Visa (e-X1 V) covers specific short-term purposes including production investments and specialized projects, granting 3-month or 6-month validity with multiple entries.

topics.title: Official Anti-Fraud Advisory on Emergency Fees
topics.summary: The Government of India charges no emergency or express processing fees and warns against unauthorized commercial websites.
topics.content: The Government of India maintains no provision for charging emergency fees, express processing surcharges, or expedited delivery costs for e-Visas. Applicants are warned that commercial websites claiming to offer guaranteed emergency or fast-track e-Visas in exchange for extra fees are unauthorized third parties. Official e-Visa fees are fixed and published directly on the portal.

topics.title: Saving and Retrieving Partially Completed Applications
topics.summary: Applicants can save draft applications and resume completion later using their unique Application ID.
topics.content: The portal supports saving unfinished forms. If an applicant cannot finish the form in one session, progress can be saved. To resume later, click 'Complete Partially Filled Application Form' on the homepage action bar and enter the system-generated Application ID provided on page one along with passport details.

topics.title: Document Verification Scrutiny and Re-upload System
topics.summary: Applications flagged for document discrepancies receive an email within 24 hours directing them to the Reupload Data tool.
topics.content: After submission, applications undergo verification scrutiny. If an uploaded photo or passport scan is blurred, unreadable, or non-compliant, the applicant receives an email notification within 24 hours. The applicant must access the 'Reupload Data' action tab on the portal homepage to upload corrected JPEG or PDF files using their Application ID and date of birth.

topics.title: Application Status Tracking and Official ETA Generation
topics.summary: Applicants can track processing status online and print their Electronic Travel Authorization prior to travel.
topics.content: Applicants can monitor processing status using the 'Check your Visa Status' button by entering their Application ID and Passport Number. Once approved (status showing 'GRANTED'), the traveler must use the 'Print e-Visa Application' feature on the homepage to generate a physical paper copy of the Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) to present at immigration checkpoints.

topics.title: Payment Gateway Processing and Transaction Verification
topics.summary: Fees are processed via SBI ePay or Axis Bank with a 3% bank charge. Use 'Verify Payment' for interrupted sessions.
topics.content: e-Visa fee payments are processed via official gateways including SBI ePay and Axis Bank, supporting international credit cards, debit cards, and digital wallets. A 3% bank charge is added to the base visa fee. If a network timeout or unconfirmed transaction occurs, applicants must use the 'Verify Payment/Pay e-Visa Fee' portal button before re-attempting payment to avoid duplicate charges.

topics.title: Designated e-Visa Air and Sea Ports of Entry
topics.summary: e-Visa holders must enter India strictly through designated airports and seaports. Departure is permitted via any authorized ICP.
topics.content: Holders of an approved ETA are restricted to entering India strictly through 28+ designated international airports (such as Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Cochin) and 5 designated seaports (Mumbai, Cochin, Goa, Mangalore, Chennai). Initial entry through land border posts is prohibited. However, foreign travelers may exit India through any authorized Immigration Check Post (ICP).

topics.title: Official 24/7 Helpdesk and Escalation Support
topics.summary: 24/7 technical and payment support lines are available via international telephone numbers and official email.
topics.content: The e-Visa portal maintains official support channels: General visa inquiries are handled 24/7 via phone at +91 82 7808 7808 and email at indian-evisa@gov.in. Dedicated payment gateway helpdesks are operated by SBI ePay (+91-022-65361671) and Axis Bank (+91 1800-419-0073), along with country-specific toll-free hotlines for US, UK, UAE, Australia, and other regions.
